mechanism: Vitamin K is a cofactor for clotting factor synthesis. High intake competes with warfarin's anticoagulant mechanism.
effect: Reduces anticoagulant effectiveness. Sudden increases in vitamin K intake can cause INR to drop.
recommendation: Maintain consistent vitamin K intake. Do not suddenly increase or eliminate high vitamin K foods. Discuss any dietary changes with your doctor.

mechanism: Calcium binds levothyroxine in the GI tract, reducing absorption.
effect: Reduced levothyroxine bioavailability, potentially leading to inadequate thyroid hormone replacement.
recommendation: Take levothyroxine 30-60 minutes before any calcium-containing food or supplement.

mechanism: Iron chelates levothyroxine in the GI tract, reducing absorption.
recommendation: Separate levothyroxine from iron-rich foods or iron supplements by at least 2-4 hours.

mechanism: Calcium competes with iron for intestinal absorption via shared divalent metal transporter.
effect: Reduced iron absorption when taken together.
recommendation: Separate iron and calcium supplements or calcium-rich foods by at least 2 hours.

mechanism: Tannins in tea and coffee chelate iron and reduce absorption.
recommendation: Avoid tea or coffee within 1 hour before or after taking iron supplements or eating iron-rich foods.

mechanism: Alcohol increases risk of lactic acidosis with metformin and can cause hypoglycemia.
effect: Risk of lactic acidosis and hypoglycemia.
recommendation: Avoid or strictly limit alcohol consumption while taking metformin.

mechanism: Grapefruit furanocoumarins inhibit CYP3A4, significantly increasing statin plasma levels.
effect: Markedly increased statin levels, raising risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
recommendation: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking atorvastatin.
